children: NVIDIA shares fell 4.3% after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and director in November. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO as the board searches for a successor.
NVIDIA (NVDA) posted Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year, and forecast $130 billion for the current quarter, above estimates. Shares fell 2.9% on November 18.
The SEC has launched an early-stage probe into NVIDIA’s accounting and whether its disclosures misled investors. It’s unclear if the inquiry is tied to alleged chip smuggling to China.
NVIDIA reported record revenue of $115.8 billion, but guidance excluded Chinese contracts amid U.S. export curbs and limits on remote chip rentals, putting potential future revenue at risk.
NVIDIA chair Harvey Jones said the company has no plans to bring Huang back. Any return would depend on an investigation into alleged leaks of company secrets and national-security concerns.
The U.S. administration announced new restrictions on how Chinese companies can access NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) chips through Southeast Asia.
NVIDIA is seeking a permanent CEO. Its recruiter reportedly approached Arm chief Rene Haas, who worked at NVIDIA for seven years before joining Arm in 2013.
U.S. lawmakers disclosed that NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) and AMD had requested export licenses covering 3.4 million AI chips, with more than 879,000 licenses approved.
NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) acquired a developer of diffusion AI technology.
Chamath Palihapitiya warned that reinstating Jensen Huang at NVIDIA could weaken governance and expose stakeholders to risk, while praising Huang’s contributions and defending CFO Colette Kress.
